bullets.text: Q3 companywide CR 91.9 (YTD 90.4), outperforming the 96 CR goal; Commercial Lines Q3 CR 93.7 (YTD 88.7, September 100.1); Property Q3 CR 102.3 (YTD 103.1) missed profitability targets.
15th consecutive quarter of double-digit NPW growth; total Q3 NPW +12% YOY (slightly slower than Q2); YTD NPW +13%; Commercial Lines NPW +11% for Q3 and +16% YTD.
Personal auto YTD frequency declined 2–3%; severity rose 6–7%, led by bodily injury (+8%); collision severity moderated to ~3% in Q3; Commercial Lines strengthened reserves in several states.
Gallup survey response reached 84%; 71% of employees engaged versus 34% nationally; achieved $1-for-$1 pay equity for women and people of color; ranked first in WSJ S&P 500 diversity and inclusion.

Property underperformed profit targets predominantly due to weather; aggregate stop loss recoverables increased by $34.6M in Q3 ($128.0M YTD); adopted severe convective storm models to guide wind and hail pricing.

Personal auto model 8.6 active in seven states; Property is increasing rates and improving price segmentation to manage hail risk; Ohio BOP rate decrease effective October is expected to yield additional volume.

Property 4.0 product model active in three states with three more planned in Q4; BOP expanding to three additional states in late 2019; Lyft TNC coverage launched in Nevada, Illinois, and Pennsylvania.

Investment portfolio earned 1.2% total return in Q3; equities returned 1.4%; reduced fixed-income credit risk while marginally increasing interest rate exposure; 2008–2018 average annual ROE was 18% versus 10% for S&P P&C Index.

CEO signed Business Roundtable Statement on the Purpose of a Corporation, reinforcing multi-stakeholder focus; Progressive Foundation and employees donated over $9.6M in 2018; Keys to Progress provided 600+ vehicles to military members.

Property 4.0 included coverage and underwriting changes requested by Platinum agents; positive agent feedback on BOP quoting and technology, alongside production and competitor analysis, informed Ohio rate level adjustments.
